Freezing existing embeddings during early domain adaptation does produce more geometrically coherent new-token representations, but the coherence is conditional on the frozen geometry being isotropic enough to provide meaningful gradient signal — and this conditionality is itself the diagnostic. The practical implication is that the correct intervention is not simply freezing but freezing combined with embedding space isotropy regularization during the joint phase, targeting the co-training interference directly rather than deferring it.
